description: Shadow Ballot is a participation-deniable private voting system on Ethereum using anamorphic signatures + stealth addresses. Voters send normal-looking ETH transfers that hide votes in the ECDSA signature nonce. A coordinator scans stealth addresses and decodes hidden votes. No voter ever touches a voting contract. Web app with voter view, coordinator view, and explorer view. Sepolia testnet. Dark theme. Hackathon project.

userStories.title: Project scaffolding and crypto library
userStories.description: Set up the project with Vite + vanilla TypeScript. Port the anamorphic ECDSA library from the existing Node.js PoC to browser-compatible code using noble-secp256k1 and js-sha3. Implement core functions: signWithCustomNonce, deriveNonceFromSecret, extractHiddenMessage, verifySignature.
acceptanceCriteria: Project initialized with Vite + TypeScript
package.json with dev, build, preview scripts
noble-secp256k1 (or @noble/secp256k1) and @noble/hashes installed for browser crypto
ethers.js v6 installed for Ethereum interactions
src/lib/anamorphic.ts implements: signWithCustomNonce(privateKey, msgHash, k) returning {r, s, recovery}
src/lib/anamorphic.ts implements: deriveNonceFromSecret(sharedSecret, publicMessage, hiddenMessage) returning bigint k
src/lib/anamorphic.ts implements: extractHiddenMessage(signature, publicMessage, sharedSecret, candidateMessages) returning matched message or null
src/lib/anamorphic.ts implements: createAnamorphicSignature(privateKey, sharedSecret, publicMessage, hiddenMessage) as high-level API
KDF uses keccak256 with counter-based rejection loop to keep k in valid range [1, n-1]
All functions work in browser (no Node.js-only dependencies)
Unit test file src/lib/anamorphic.test.ts with at least 3 tests: sign+verify, sign+extract hidden message, normal vs anamorphic indistinguishability
npm run dev serves the page, npm run build produces static output
userStories.notes: Reference implementation at ~/Projects/anamorphic-signatures-poc/anamorphic-ecdsa.js. Port the logic but use noble-secp256k1 instead of elliptic.js for smaller bundle. The core trick: k = KDF(sharedSecret, messageHash, hiddenData) instead of random. Extraction is brute-force: try each candidate, derive k, compute r, check if it matches signature r.

userStories.title: Stealth address generation and scanning
userStories.description: Implement simplified ERC-5564 stealth addresses. The coordinator publishes a stealth meta-address (spending + viewing public keys). Voters generate one-time stealth addresses using ECDH. The coordinator scans transactions to detect which ones were sent to their stealth addresses.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/stealth.ts implements stealth meta-address generation: generateStealthKeys() returning {spendingKey, viewingKey, spendingPubKey, viewingPubKey, metaAddress}
src/lib/stealth.ts implements: generateStealthAddress(metaAddress) returning {stealthAddress, ephemeralPubKey, sharedSecret}
src/lib/stealth.ts implements: scanForStealthTx(viewingPrivKey, spendingPubKey, ephemeralPubKey, txRecipient) returning boolean
src/lib/stealth.ts implements: computeStealthPrivateKey(spendingPrivKey, viewingPrivKey, ephemeralPubKey) for coordinator to spend received funds
ECDH shared secret: s = ephemeralPrivKey * viewingPubKey (sender side) = viewingPrivKey * ephemeralPubKey (receiver side)
Stealth address derivation: stealthAddr = pubKeyToAddress(spendingPubKey + hash(sharedSecret) * G)
Meta-address format: concatenation of spending and viewing public keys (hex string)
Unit tests: generate stealth address, scan and detect it, verify non-matching tx rejected
All crypto uses noble-secp256k1, works in browser
userStories.notes: Simplified ERC-5564. Skip view tags for now. The coordinator will scan ALL transactions to their stealth addresses by trying each ephemeral public key. For the hackathon demo this is fine since we'll have <100 transactions.

userStories.title: Raw transaction signing with custom nonce and broadcasting
userStories.description: Implement raw Ethereum transaction construction and signing that uses our custom ECDSA nonce k (for anamorphic signatures) instead of the standard random nonce. Support broadcasting to Sepolia via public RPC. This is the critical bridge between our crypto library and the Ethereum network.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/tx.ts implements: buildTransaction(from, to, value, nonce, chainId) returning unsigned tx object
src/lib/tx.ts implements: signTransactionWithCustomK(unsignedTx, privateKey, customK) returning signed raw tx hex
src/lib/tx.ts implements: broadcastTransaction(signedTxHex) returning tx hash
src/lib/tx.ts implements: getTransactionCount(address) for nonce management
Transaction is EIP-1559 type (type 2) for Sepolia compatibility
Signing produces valid v, r, s values that Ethereum nodes accept
The custom k is used instead of RFC 6979 deterministic nonce
RPC calls use public Sepolia endpoints (e.g., https://rpc.sepolia.org, https://ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com)
Fallback to multiple RPC URLs if one fails
Integration test: sign a tx with custom k, verify the signature is valid, verify r value matches expected
Error handling for insufficient funds, nonce too low, tx rejected
userStories.notes: This is the hardest part. ethers.js Transaction class handles RLP encoding but uses its own signing. We need to: 1) Build the unsigned tx with ethers, 2) Get the tx hash to sign, 3) Sign with our custom k using noble-secp256k1, 4) Inject our r,s,v back into the tx, 5) Serialize and broadcast. Alternatively, do all RLP encoding manually. Test carefully on Sepolia.

userStories.title: Vote encoding, end-to-end voting flow, and wallet management
userStories.description: Implement the complete voting pipeline: wallet generation, vote encoding, anamorphic tx creation with stealth addresses, and coordinator-side vote extraction. This combines all crypto primitives into the full Shadow Ballot flow.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/wallet.ts implements: generateWallet() returning {privateKey, publicKey, address} stored in localStorage
src/lib/wallet.ts implements: loadOrCreateWallet() that persists across sessions
src/lib/vote.ts implements: encodeVote(proposalId, choice) returning vote_data bytes (proposalId 1 byte + vote 1 byte: 0x01=YES, 0x02=NO, 0x03=ABSTAIN)

src/lib/vote.ts implements: castVote(voterPrivKey, coordinatorMetaAddress, sharedSecret, proposalId, choice) that: generates stealth address, builds 0.001 ETH transfer tx, signs with anamorphic nonce encoding the vote, returns {txHash, ephemeralPubKey}

src/lib/vote.ts implements: decodeVote(coordinatorViewingKey, coordinatorSpendingPubKey, ephemeralPubKey, txSignature, txHash, sharedSecret, proposalIds) that: verifies stealth address match, extracts hidden vote via brute-force over candidates
Candidate set for extraction: for N proposals, try each proposalId with YES/NO/ABSTAIN = 3N candidates
Shared secret between voter and coordinator is derived from ECDH (ephemeral key exchange) — NOT pre-shared
End-to-end test: castVote() produces a tx, decodeVote() extracts the correct proposalId and choice
Console logging for each step to aid debugging during demo
userStories.notes: The shared secret for the anamorphic signature should be derived from the same ECDH used for stealth addresses. The ephemeral key serves double duty: it generates the stealth address AND provides the shared secret for hiding the vote. This is elegant — one key exchange, two privacy properties.

userStories.title: Smart contract deployment (ShadowBallot.sol)
userStories.description: Write and deploy a minimal Solidity contract to Sepolia that stores voting proposals and aggregated results. Only the coordinator can submit results. No voter ever interacts with this contract.
acceptanceCriteria: contracts/ShadowBallot.sol with: createProposal(string title, uint256 deadline) returning proposalId
submitResults(uint256 proposalId, uint256 yesVotes, uint256 noVotes, uint256 abstainVotes) — onlyCoordinator modifier
getProposal(uint256 proposalId) returning (title, deadline, yesVotes, noVotes, abstainVotes, finalized)
getProposalCount() returning total number of proposals
Coordinator address set in constructor, immutable
Events: ProposalCreated(proposalId, title, deadline), ResultsSubmitted(proposalId, yes, no, abstain)
Contract deployed to Sepolia testnet
Deployed address saved in src/config.ts along with ABI
src/lib/contract.ts with helper functions: createProposal(), submitResults(), getProposal(), getProposalCount()
Hardhat or Foundry config for compilation and deployment (builder's choice)
Deployment script that deploys and saves address
userStories.notes: Keep the contract dead simple. It's just a results registry. The privacy happens off-chain in the signatures. Use a fresh Sepolia deployer wallet — get testnet ETH from a faucet. If faucets are unreliable, hardcode a pre-deployed contract address instead and skip deployment automation.

userStories.title: Voter view — proposal list and vote casting
userStories.description: Build the voter view where users see active proposals, click to vote YES/NO/ABSTAIN, and the app handles the full anamorphic voting flow behind the scenes. Show transaction confirmation with Etherscan link.
acceptanceCriteria: Voter view loads proposals from the smart contract (or hardcoded list for demo)
Each proposal shows: title, deadline, voting buttons (YES / NO / ABSTAIN)
Wallet auto-generated on first visit, address displayed in header with copy button
Balance check: show current Sepolia ETH balance, warn if insufficient for voting (needs ~0.002 ETH per vote)
Clicking a vote button triggers the full flow: generate stealth address → sign anamorphic tx → broadcast
Loading state during tx signing and broadcasting (spinner + status messages)
On success: show tx hash with clickable Etherscan Sepolia link
Success message emphasizes privacy: 'Your vote was cast as a normal ETH transfer. No one can tell you voted.'
On failure: show error message with retry option
Voted proposals marked as 'Vote Cast' (prevent double voting from UI)
Console logs the ephemeral public key and stealth address for debugging
userStories.notes: For the demo, pre-create 2-3 proposals. The Etherscan link is the key demo moment — when opened, it should look like a completely normal 0.001 ETH transfer with no voting contract in sight. Pre-fund 3-5 voter wallets with Sepolia ETH for smooth demo.

userStories.title: Coordinator view — scan, decode, and tally
userStories.description: Build the coordinator view where the trusted coordinator scans for incoming stealth transactions, decodes hidden votes from anamorphic signatures, displays the tally, and can submit aggregated results on-chain.
acceptanceCriteria: Coordinator view requires entering coordinator private key (or loaded from config for demo)
Scan button that checks recent Sepolia transactions for stealth address matches
For each detected stealth tx: display tx hash, sender address, and decoded vote (proposalId + YES/NO/ABSTAIN)
Vote tally displayed per proposal: YES count, NO count, ABSTAIN count, total
Visual indicator showing decode status (scanning... → found N votes → decoded)
Submit Results button that calls the smart contract's submitResults()
After submission: show on-chain tx hash confirming results were posted
Scanning uses Sepolia block explorer API or RPC eth_getLogs to find relevant transactions
The ephemeral public keys are stored/announced somewhere the coordinator can find them (localStorage shared state for demo, or a simple announcement mechanism)
Error handling for: no transactions found, decode failures, contract submission failures
userStories.notes: For the hackathon demo, the simplest announcement mechanism is: voter writes {txHash, ephemeralPubKey} to a shared in-memory store or localStorage. In production this would be an on-chain announcement log (ERC-5564 style). The coordinator needs ephemeral pub keys to scan — without them, scanning requires checking every single transaction.

userStories.title: Explorer view — decode any transaction
userStories.description: Build the explorer view: the 'holy shit' demo moment. Paste any voting tx hash, see what it looks like on Etherscan (normal transfer), then decode the hidden vote. Side-by-side comparison.
acceptanceCriteria: Text input to paste a transaction hash
Fetch transaction details from Sepolia RPC (to, from, value, input data, signature r,s,v)
Left panel: 'What the world sees' — displays the tx as it appears publicly: a simple ETH transfer between two addresses, value, gas, block number
Right panel: 'What's actually hidden' — decoded vote: proposal title, vote choice (YES/NO/ABSTAIN), voter's ephemeral key
Visual transition/reveal animation between the two views (e.g., click 'Decode' button and the hidden content fades in)
If tx is not a Shadow Ballot vote: show 'This transaction does not contain a hidden vote' gracefully
Decode requires the shared secret — for demo, use the coordinator's keys from config
Link to view on Etherscan Sepolia for verification ('See for yourself — it's just a transfer')
Styled dramatically: the reveal should feel like peeling back a layer
userStories.notes: This is the demo climax. The judge sees a boring Etherscan transfer, then the app reveals it's actually a vote. The contrast between the two views should be stark and memorable. Consider a dramatic reveal animation — maybe a 'decrypt' visual effect.

userStories.notes: The demo flow for judges: 1) Show voter view, cast a vote, 2) Open Etherscan — it's just a transfer, 3) Switch to coordinator view — vote appears decoded, 4) Switch to explorer view — paste the tx hash, see the reveal. This should take 2-3 minutes and be seamless. Pre-fund enough wallets that you don't hit faucet issues during the live demo.
